To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the SWCNT–liquid crystal elastomer nanocomposite films exhibit reversible white light-induced deformation.

the SWCNT incorporated LCE nanocomposite film demonstrated strong, reversible photo-actuation under irradiation of white-light, and the nematic–Isotropic transition temperature was evidently lower than that for the blank LCE.

the incorporation of single-walled carbon nanotubes into liquid crystalline elastomers enables white-light actuation, which can be applied for the development of novel actuators and artificial muscles.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and fabrication of SWCNT–LCO nanocomposites that exhibit reversible white-light actuation, which may be applied to the development of new types of smart materials and nanodevices.
the development of a novel type of white-light actuated SWCNT–LCO nanocomposites that can be used for various applications such as artificial muscles, micro-robots, and micro-actuators.

the development of photo-actuated nanocomposites that can be actuated with visible light, and the results are expected to be useful for applications in the fields of optoelectronic devices and soft actuators.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the incorporation of SWCNTs into the nematic liquid crystalline polymer matrix can effectively enhance the photoactuation of the resultant nanocomposite films.
the SWCNTs are effective at absorbing and dissipating the energy of white light, which can be utilized for photoactuation.

the SWCNT–nematic LCE nanocomposites are capable of reversible photoactuation under white-light irradiation, and that the SWCNT incorporation is a promising method for the development of photoactuation materials.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
SWCNTs can effectively lower the nematic–iso transition temperatures of nematic LCEs by up to 20 °C.
SWCNT incorporated nematic LCE nanocomposites are able to actuate in response to both IR and white light.
SWCNT–LCP nanocomposites can be used for white-light-driven actuation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
SWCNTs can be used to enhance the photoactuation ability of LCEs and that the photoactuation is not limited to IR irradiation.
the photoinduced actuation can be achieved in a broad range of wavelengths by using the nanocomposites.
the incorporation of a small quantity of SWCNTs into LCE materials is an effective approach to achieve reversible white-light actuation.
